text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up: eu-west1 GPU pool is spiking — ~120 pods pending right now. A lot of them pinned with nodeSelector gpu-type=A100 + strict zone anti-affinity. Noticed a wave of spot node reclaimed events around 12:40UTC.
Ajay Patel: Seen similar. Any autoscaler / instance group correlation? :thinking:
Maria Chen: Autoscaler logs show quick scale-downs then immediate scale-ups. nodepool-eu-west1-spot had ~12 terminations in 5m. Scheduler backlog shows many high-priority pods stuck in Pending binding phase.
Taylor Kim: Pasting one pending pod describe for context:
```
Name: ml-train-42
Namespace: prod-ml
Status: Pending
Events:
  2m  default-scheduler  0/50 nodes are available: 50 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 18 Insufficient memory.
```
Prashant Singh: That taint line stands out — we only taint spot nodes as `spot=true:NoSchedule`. Are these pods tolerating spot? If not, when spots go away the scheduler refuses to place on on-demand nodes because of additional required affinities.
Maria Chen: Exactly. Most of these pods have requiredDuringScheduling for gpu-type=A100 and required anti-affinity across `zone` to spread jobs. Combined with spot taints, there is zero compatible node when spots drop.
Ajay Patel: Can we add a fallback affinity rule? Like prefer A100 but allow V100 with a lower score, or add a `fallback=true` label to tolerate on-demand. That would save a ton of churn.
Taylor Kim: Note: we rolled a small scheduler plugin tweak yesterday that tightened topologySpread for GPU workloads. Could be the regression making the scheduler overly strict.
oncall-sre: deploy-bot triggered autoscaler:provision at 12:41UTC — provisioning ondemand nodes to help. ETA ~6m.
Maria Chen: Thanks. Cost note: switching to ondemand for the burst will bump cost ~30% for the window. We should do it short-lived then revert.
Prashant Singh: Short-term mitigation path: open a small scheduler override for pods labeled `cohort=best-effort` that relaxes the taint/affinity predicate. I'll draft a canary PR that only affects non-critical training jobs.
Taylor Kim: Also we should validate yesterday's topoSpread change — if revert fixes it we cut a new release.
Maria Chen: For immediate triage: 1) Ajay to patch a fallback affinity (gpu-type preferred, not required) for models that can degrade to V100. 2) Prashant to open scheduler canary PR relaxing taint enforcement for `cohort=best-effort`. 3) Taylor to test revert of topologySpread change in a canary cluster. If still bad, we'll run emergency steady-state ondemand scale for 1 hour.
Ajay Patel: I can push the affinity patch now and monitor binding. Will also add metric alerts for fallback usage.
Prashant Singh: PR opened: #8212 (canary). It relaxes the `NoSchedule` check for `cohort=best-effort` pods at scheduling time only.
deploy-bot: autoscaler:provision completed — 4 ondemand nodes added to eu-west1 pool.
oncall-sre: Update: 40 pods bound after new nodes, ~22 still pending (mostly due to strict zone anti-affinity). Continuing to debug placement scoring.
Maria Chen: Good progress. Keep cost / eviction metrics visible. Once Ajay's patch lands we can shift pending ones to fallback affinity and drain spot churn.
Ajay Patel: ack — rolling the patch now, will post binding numbers in 5m.
Taylor Kim: ack. If canary fails I will rollback the topoSpread change.
Prashant Singh: ack. Also adding a quick script to retag a small subset of pending pods with `cohort=best-effort` so scheduler can place them as a one-off.
Maria Chen: Thanks all. Postmortem capture: spike caused by simultaneous spot reclamation + recent topoSpread tightening + strict required GPU affinity. Action items: fallback affinity, scheduler canary, revert topoSpread if needed, short ondemand burst during recovery.
Ajay Patel: noted
Taylor Kim: noted
Prashant Singh: noted
